summary: Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1985–1986), Harvard University (~1989–1992), and under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

Hyoung Seok Ham works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Virginia (2010) and earned a PhD from the University of Michigan, supervised by Madhav M. Deshpande, also studying under Donald S. Lopez, Jr.

Hywel David Lewis (1910–1992) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Ysgol Syr Hugh Owen, Bangor University (~1928–1932), and Jesus College, Oxford (~1932–1935), later holding a post at Bangor University (~1936–1955).

Hürelbaatar Ujeed is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge and holds a post as Professor and Principle Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.
Hōin Yamada (born 1940) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University and studied under Gyōin Hashimoto.
Hōju (born 1980) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University and KU Leuven. Kyokuga Saeki was among his students.

Ian Harris (1952–2014) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge and Lancaster, founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies, and held positions at St Martin's College (~1986–2007) and the University of Cumbria (attested 2000–2014).

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University by 2004 and was attested in 2005 as a research fellow at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute.
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saitama University and under Sotan Oka. He later taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani.

Ian Mabbett (1939–2020) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Oxford. He served as Reader in History at Monash University (~1965–2004) and Professor at Aichi Bunkyo University (2000).

Ian Reader (born 1949) specializes in religious studies and Japanology. After earning his doctorate from the University of Leeds, he held posts at the University of Stirling (~1989–1999), University of Hawaiʻi (~1999–2000), and Lancaster University (~1999–2006).

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeologist who earned his PhD from the University of Peshawar (by 2007), studying under Farid Khan, Taj Ali, and Ihsan Ali. He became Associate Professor and Department Chairman at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa (born 1936) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959) and later served as university president there (~1966–2004), as well as holding posts at other affiliated institutions.

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) studied religious studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology at First Higher School and the University of Tokyo under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Tohoku University (~1952–1965) and the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama (born 1942) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Komazawa and Otani Universities under Kogen Mizuno, later serving as an associate professor at Komazawa University (1975–2013) and visiting scholar at Oxford and Sun Yat-sen University.
Ichisada Miyazaki (1901–1995) was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University under Jitsuzo Kuwabara (~1922–1925) and later held an academic post at Kyoto University (~1936–1965).
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) studied at the University of Rome, where he later served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University (~1935–1940), he held a long-term post at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1960–1998).

Ihsan Ali (born 1955) is an archaeology and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Peshawar and under Raymond Allchin, later serving as Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009) and Professor at the University of Peshawar.

Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Komazawa University. Arai was supervised for the MA by Shiro Matsumoto and studied under Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.
